newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand ended firm but retraced from its best levels towards the close on dollar short-covering, dealers said.
They said players began squaring positions after earlier going short on dollars amid rumours of a large offshore dollar sell order in the market.
"A lot of people went short this morning on what looked like a big order from offshore to sell dollars. This started the rand's spiral to stronger levels," a dealer said.
"But towards the close the order looked like it was finished and people rushed to square off their positions."
The local unit closed at 4.5100/50 against the dollar from a Tuesday finish of 4.5365/5415 close, after touching a best level of 4.5030 bid during the day.
Dealers said a continued flow of dollars in the late afternoon kept the rand from weakening further just before the finish.
"There were still dollars coming in at the 4.52 level," a trader said.
They said the rand would look to stage an assault on the 4.50 resistance level on Thursday.
"4.50 is the level to watch tommorrow (Thursday). But the rand will not come screaming down. I see 4.50 as the bottom end of the trading range and 4.54 the top," a dealer said.
Traders said a breach of the 4.50 level would see the rand head lower.
"If the rand breaks 4.50, which is going to be difficult to get through, 4.48 could be the next big one," a dealer said.
Against the crosses the local unit firmed to last trade at 7.0593/0717 from 7.0864/0987 against sterling late on Tuesday and at 0.3386/3391 from 0.3361/3366 marks previously.
Key long bonds ended robust tracking a stronger rand and U.S. gilt market, dealers said.
"The U.S. T-bond is firm, our market is looking strong technically and the rand is strong," a dealer said.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was last at 6.86 percent down from 6.88 percent overnight when the market rallied following the release of surprisingly weak U.S. economic data.

Dealers said the market had also been boosted by comments from Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals who on Tuesday night said he would not decrease interest rates until South Africa's import and current account improved.
The key R150 was last at 15.185 pct from 15.305 at 1400 GMT on Tuesday after struggling to decisively pierce 15.20 pct throughout the day.
Dealers said a breach of this key technical level would see bonds move stronger.
"15.20 percent has proved to be a tough resistance level, but if it is broken decisively rates could head down to around 15.11," a dealer said.
Dealers said trade during the afternoon had been sporadic after busy dealings earlier in the day. "It comes in bursts, suddenly really busy and then fairly quiet for a while."
Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners bought a net 223.31 million rand worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after buying a net 58.59 million rand on Monday.
Nominal cumulative volumes amounted to 5.61 billion rand from 4.79 billion rand on Monday.
On the money market, three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.70 to 15.90 percent, while 90-day BAs were unchanged at 15.15 to 15.30 percent.
The Reserve Bank quoted the daily shortage around 400 million rand lower at 8.869 billion rand on Tuesday from 9.282 billion rand on Monday.
-- Nicole Mordant, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
